articles.title: Angel Reese, Dream Beat Valkyries in WNBA Finals Game 2, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Top Players
articles.summary: Home-court advantage in the 2026 WNBA Finals now belongs to the Atlanta Dream.
articles.body:
Home-court advantage in the 2026 WNBA Finals now belongs to the Atlanta Dream.

Angel Reese and the Dream came into the Chase Center on Monday and left with a commanding 79-65 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 to tie the series at one apiece.

The Dream have plenty of momentum as the series shifts to Atlanta in large part because of Reese's individual brilliance during a historic performance. She was unguardable down low, dominant on the boards and her usual self on defense, while Allisha Gray provided important scoring as well.

Enes Kanter Freedom Says He Will Attend WNBA Finals Game 3 in Atlanta (AP)

Golden State was unable to overcome Gabby Williams' shooting struggles (3-of-15 from the field) and had no answer for the visitors.

Game 1 was a defensive battle with the Valkyries taking over in crunch time and limiting the Dream to a mere eight points in the fourth quarter. That put the Atlanta offense firmly under the spotlight for Game 2 since it could have stolen one on the road with even an average offensive performance at the end of that first contest.

And the visitors responded in the early going by taking a two-point halftime lead.

Reese matched those eight points in the first quarter by herself and had 15 at intermission by doing a little bit of everything. She got out in transition, created opportunities in half-court sets with her rim-running and finished through contact all while battling for boards and protecting the rim on the defensive side.

Her initial impact was particularly important because Rhyne Howard picked up her fourth foul in the second quarter. That put more of the onus on everyone else, and Gray also helped carry the offense by hitting from the outside when defenders collapsed on Reese in the paint.

Still, Golden State was well within striking distance with Tiffany Hayes providing a spark off the bench to help make up for Williams' shooting woes as the star did much of her scoring from the free-throw line.

But striking distance disappeared during the first real separation of the game when Atlanta closed the third quarter on a 15-2 run.

Reese was the driving force behind the spurt with six of the points, an assist and a steal, but it was Jordin Canada who added the exclamation mark by banking in a long-range three as time expired.

Atlanta's defense was also not to be overlooked, as it held the Valkyries to a paltry nine points in the quarter. Williams couldn't get anything going after playing so well in Game 1, which stifled nearly everything Golden State tried on the offensive side.

The fourth quarter was largely a formality with the Dream in full control, although it was fitting it was Reese who hit a three with fewer than five minutes remaining to push the advantage back to 19 after Golden State built slight momentum.

She was the best player on the floor and took over whenever needed for a team that will now return home for an important Game 3 on Wednesday.

articles.title: Angel Reese gets 30 points, 16 rebounds as Dream beat Valkyries 79-65 to even WNBA Finals at 1-1
articles.summary: Atlanta earned the franchise’s first Finals victory after going winless in three previous trips — 0-10 overall.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO — Angel Reese had 30 points and 16 rebounds, Allisha Gray added 18 points and the Atlanta Dream stymied Golden State on both ends in the second half, beating the Valkyries 79-65 on Monday night to even the best-of-seven WNBA Finals at one game apiece. Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals, while Jordin Canada contributed 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds as the Dream earned the franchise's first Finals victory after going winless in three previous trips — 0-10 overall. They now head home having salvaged a split in front of the boisterous “Ballhalla” crowd at Chase Center. Reese became the third player with at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game, joining Jonquel Jones for Connecticut in 2019 and Breanna Stewart for Seattle in 2020. Game 3 is Wednesday in Atlanta, where the next two matchups were moved to the NBA Hawks’ State Farm Arena so more fans could attend. It holds more than 17,000, as opposed to the Dream’s regular home, Gateway Center Arena, which accommodates only 3,500. Chase Center holds 18,064 and has sold out every game since the Valkyries began playing last year. Gabby Williams finished with 14 points on 3-for-15 shooting after she was the only Golden State player to score in double figures with 26 points in Saturday’s 68-64 Game 1 win. Foul trouble almost did in the Dream this time — but Reese simply wouldn’t have it. She went scoreless in the second half of the opener but delivered the big baskets and key defensive stops two days later, finishing 10 for 16 from the floor while dishing out three assists and blocking two shots. Atlanta scored 24 points off Golden State's 19 turnovers to hand the Valkyries their first loss in regulation since a 73-70 defeat at Chicago on Aug. 21.

articles.title: 'I Was Hungry,' Angel Reese Reacts to Historic Performance in Dream Win vs. Valkyries in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream's Game 1 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the 2026 WNBA Finals was a motivating factor for Angel Reese in Monday's 79-65 victory in Game 2.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream's Game 1 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the 2026 WNBA Finals was a motivating factor for Angel Reese in Monday's 79-65 victory in Game 2.

"I was hungry," she told reporters after leading the Dream to their first WNBA Finals win in franchise history (36:40 mark). "I wanted one. I think we let one slip away. And you can't do that, especially on the road in a good environment against a good team.

"We all came together and were pissed. We felt disappointed. We felt embarrassed. We didn't like the outcome of that last game, and we didn't want to let another one slip."

Enes Kanter Freedom Says He Will Attend WNBA Finals Game 3 in Atlanta (AP)

Atlanta led Game 1 by five points heading into the fourth quarter but managed to score just eight total points in the last quarter as Golden State earned the win.

There would be no such missed opportunities for the visitors in Game 2, though, as they finished the third quarter on a 15-2 run to seize a double-digit advantage and never looked back during a fourth quarter that ended up being largely a formality.

Reese was the driving force behind the win and finished with 30 points, 16 rebounds, three assists and two blocks in a dominant performance.

She joined Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones as the only players in WNBA history to finish with 30 or more points and 15 or more rebounds in a Finals game. The Dream turned to her whenever they needed a basket all while she provided her normal stifling defense on the other end.

The LSU product got out in transition, scored on the blocks and even hit a three-pointer in the fourth quarter as Atlanta turned away any late spurts from the Valkyries.

It wasn't just Reese, as Allisha Gray drilled three triples on her way to 18 points. Jordin Canada added 13 points, three of which came on a banked three-pointer to end that decisive third quarter.

The Atlanta defense also set the tone and held Gabby Williams to 3-of-15 shooting from the field. Golden State as a whole shot an ugly 34 percent from the field with 18 turnovers and failed to generate enough open looks to keep pace with Reese's unstoppable performance.

Now the series shifts to Atlanta for Wednesday's Game 3 with all the momentum on the Dream's side thanks in large part to Reese.

articles.title: Angel Reese reina en la Finales de la WNBA: las Dream doblegan a las Valkyries y ponen el 1-1
articles.standfirst: Tras la victoria de las Dream, y con la serie abierta (1-1), ambos equipos de verán las caras el próximo miércoles en Atlanta
articles.summary: Tras la victoria de las Dream, y con la serie abierta (1-1), ambos equipos de verán las caras el próximo miércoles en Atlanta
articles.body: Las Atlanta Dream doblegaron a las Golden State Valkyries por 65-79 en el segundo juego de las finales de la WNBA, impulsadas por una brillante actuación de Angel Reese en el Chase Center de San Francisco, en el estado de California, que empata la serie. Las Valkyries dominaron por la mínima (21-18) el primer tramo del encuentro frente a unas Dream impulsadas por la intensidad de la estadounidense Angel Reese, quien aportó ocho puntos clave y que acabó el partido como la máxima anotadora con 30 puntos (16 de 10 en tiro). Sin embargo, al término de la primera mitad, la balanza se inclinó por 37-39 a favor del conjunto de las de Atlanta, que tomaron la delantera aprovechando un flojo desempeño ofensivo de las de San Francisco, que registraron un 23 % de efectividad en tiros de campo. El conjunto del este de Estados Unidos intensificó el ritmo en el tercer parcial y estiró la diferencia hasta los doce puntos en los últimos suspiros. Tras el descanso, las Dream consolidaron la brecha aprovechando una falta sobre Reese y un espectacular triple sobre la bocina de Jordin Canada que dejó el marcador en 46-60 al término del periodo. El equipo visitante mantuvo el control del juego gracias a una sólida efectividad desde la línea de tiros libres, que alcanzó el 100 %, contrastando con las dificultades ofensivas de las californianas. Reese se echó al equipo en el último cuarto para seguir agrandando las distancias frente en el último cuarto, con una diferencia de 14 puntos que mantiene en vivo la competición por el título más grande la WNBA y dejó sin contestación a las de California en su propio territorio. Las Valkyries ganaron el primer asalto por un ajustado 68-64 que se disputó el pasado sábado en San Francisco. Tras la victoria de las Dream, y con la serie abierta, ambos equipos de verán las caras el próximo miércoles en Atlanta.

articles.title: Los Lakers despiden a Dalton Knecht y retienen a Broony, el hijo de LeBron James
articles.standfirst: Tanto Knecht como Jaden Hardy y Bronny James eran los jugadores cuya continuidad peligraba entre las filas de los Lakers
articles.summary: Tanto Knecht como Jaden Hardy y Bronny James eran los jugadores cuya continuidad peligraba entre las filas de los Lakers
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers anunciaron la salida del escolta Dalton Knecht y ratificaron a Broony James, hijo de la estrella LeBron James, en la plantilla oficial, como parte del último recorte necesario de cara a la nueva temporada de la NBA que comienza esta semana. El equipo angelino liberó a Knecht dos temporadas después de su fichaje en el 'draft', en lo que prometía ser uno de los mejores movimientos del mercado. La salida del escolta estadounidense como agente libre deja a los oro y púrpura, liderados en esta nueva era por el esloveno Luka Doncic, con los 15 jugadores reglamentarios en la plantilla que permite la NBA para el inicio de la temporada regular. Tanto Knecht como Jaden Hardy y Bronny James eran los jugadores cuya continuidad peligraba entre las filas de los Lakers, debido a que sus contratos eran los más vulnerables frente al límite reglamentario de la plantilla. El equipo angelino inicia el próximo miércoles su andadura por la NBA en el estadio Crypto.com Arena de Los Ángeles contra los Golden State Warriors de Stephen Curry.

articles.title: Muere con 17 años Anna Mellano, gran promeda del baloncesto en Italia
articles.standfirst: La jugadora del Basket Venaria ha fallecido a causa de una enfermedad incurable que la había obligado a dejar las canchas de baloncesto
articles.summary: La jugadora del Basket Venaria ha fallecido a causa de una enfermedad incurable que la había obligado a dejar las canchas de baloncesto
articles.body: Anna Mellano, una de las grandes promesas del baloncesto italiano, ha muerto con 17 años. La Federación Italiana de Baloncesto (FIP) dio a conocer la noticia del fallecimiento de la joven jugadora formada en el Basket Venaria y que era internacional en categorías inferiores con Italia: "Anna Mellano ha fallecido a los 17 años. Se la ha llevado una enfermedad cruel, contra la cual luchó con la misma determinación que siempre mostró en la cancha de baloncesto". El presidente de la Federación, Giovanni Petrucci, expresó personalmente sus condolencias a sus padres, Danilo y Marta, así como al club Basket Venaria: "Para Anna, quien deja un vacío irreparable en los corazones de sus compañeras, entrenadores y aficionados, va el abrazo cariñoso de toda la comunidad del baloncesto italiano".

articles.title: Jaden McDaniels agrees to contract extension with Timberwolves. Here are the numbers
articles.summary: Jaden McDaniels is now signed with Minnesota through the 2029-30 campaign. The wing agreed to a one-year, $40 million extension with the Timberwolves on Mond...
articles.body:
Jaden McDaniels is now signed with Minnesota through the 2029-30 campaign.

The wing agreed to a one-year, $40 million extension with the Timberwolves on Monday, a source confirmed. McDaniels still had three years remaining on his current deal, making him the first player in NBA history to get an extension with that much time left on a non-max deal, per HoopsHype insider Michael Scotto.

That $40 million salary is projected to be roughly 21% of the salary cap for the 2029-30 season, which is akin to approximately Rudy Gobert's salary cap percentage this season.

McDaniels will now be eligible to sign a three-year, $180 million max deal in 2028, should both sides agree to such a contract.

So the extension sets McDaniels up to make more money on future deals, while Minnesota gets another year locked in for its two-way wing on what could be a relatively team-friendly contract when the time comes.

McDaniels averaged 14.8 points last season while shooting 51% from the floor and 41% from distance. He's an All-NBA Defense caliber stopper who's long been Minnesota's perimeter lockdown guy.

"I love Jaden," new Wolves point guard LaMelo Ball said Monday. "I mean, 6-10, can move, long, play defense, cut backdoor, shoot the three. I mean, really anything you need. It's like a damn near 2K player. It's crazy."
